title: Iterative population PK modeling with poppkflow
text: Population pharmacokinetic (popPK) model development rarely straight line. practice, analyst moves repeatedly around loop: Specify candidate model (compartment structure, absorption, random effects, residual error, covariate relationships, initial estimates). Fit model analysis dataset. Diagnose fit using numerical summaries, rule-based checks, goodness--fit plots. Compare candidate parent model (change objective function value, parameter stability, precision, shrinkage). Decide whether accept reject candidate, recording . Modify accepted model propose next candidate. ad-hoc script workflows, model code copied edited hand across numbered scripts (run001.R, run002.R, …), failed attempts disappear, parent-child relationships live spreadsheets, rationale rejected branches reconstructed weeks later reporting. poppkflow turns loop explicit, auditable data structure backed nlmixr2: Declarative specifications (pk_spec()): models R objects edited composable verbs (pk_add_iiv(), pk_set_block(), pk_add_cov(), …) compiled deterministically nlmixr2 code (pk_compile(), pk_code()). Automatic lineage (pk_candidate): editing existing run returns candidate remembers parent_id, fitting records parent computes dOFV automatically. hub--spoke run ledger: every call pk_run() writes one summary row ledger/runs.csv, appends timestamped entries ledger/events.csv, stores run artifacts models/<run_id>/. Lightweight results (result.rds) extracted immediately history, diagnostics, flags, comparison, reporting never reload full nlmixr2 fit objects (fit.rds). Standard diagnostics, evaluation, reporting: flags, suggestions, covariate screening, stepwise covariate modeling (SCM), multi-start reproducibility checks, bootstrap, VPC, exposure derivation, HTML/PDF/Word reports read directly ledger. tutorial walks complete analysis project creation final report using simulated oral PK dataset bundled package.

title: Iterative population PK modeling with poppkflow
text: Built-specifications support 1- 2-compartment linear models (linCmt()) "oral" (first-order absorption) "iv" dosing optional absorption lag time (lag = TRUE, oral ): 1-compartment oral: ka, cl, v (plus tlag lag = TRUE) 2-compartment oral: ka, cl, v2, q, v3 (plus tlag lag = TRUE) IV routes: omit ka tlag Every structural parameter parameterized log scale: Pi=exp⁡(θlog⁡P+covariate termsi+ηP,+IOV termsi,k)P_i = \exp\!\left(\theta_{\log P} + \text{covariate terms}_i + \eta_{P,} + \text{IOV terms}_{,k}\right) Initial estimates inits supplied natural scale (example, cl = 5 compiles lcl <- log(5)). Residual error can "prop", "add", "comb". pk_code() shows exact nlmixr2 function produced pk_compile(). generated text pk_run() writes models/<run_id>/model.txt hashes spec_hash:
code: spec_1cmt <- pk_spec(   ncmt = 1,   route = "oral",   lag = FALSE,   iiv = c("cl", "v"),   error = "prop",   inits = list(ka = 1, cl = 5, v = 30, prop.sd = 0.2) ) spec_1cmt #> <pk_spec>: 1-compartment, oral #> IIV: "cl" and "v"; blocks: 0; IOV: none #> Residual error: "prop" #> Covariates: none pk_params(spec_1cmt) #> [1] "ka" "cl" "v" cat(pk_code(spec_1cmt)) #> function() { #>   ini({ #>     lka <- log(1) #>     lcl <- log(5) #>     lv <- log(30) #>     eta.cl ~ 0.1 #>     eta.v ~ 0.1 #>     prop.sd <- 0.2 #>   }) #>   model({ #>     ka <- exp(lka) #>     cl <- exp(lcl + eta.cl) #>     v <- exp(lv + eta.v) #>     linCmt() ~ prop(prop.sd) #>   }) #> }

what: Choosing an estimation strategy with pk_est()
title: Iterative population PK modeling with poppkflow
text: pk_est() builds estimation settings object passed pk_run(), filling unspecified arguments config.yml. Three methods supported: "saem_focei" (default): runs SAEM first locate population optimum consistent individual modes, refines fit FOCEI started SAEM solution. oral PK data slow absorption (flip-flop tendencies), individual likelihood surfaces can multimodal; FOCEI alone may converge different local modes depending initial values, whereas SAEM→FOCEI stabilizes FOCEI objective function value (OFV) covariance step (r,s). "focei": direct FOCEI estimation. Fast convenient rapid structural exploration well-behaved datasets. "saem": SAEM alone (useful bootstrap replicates exact FOCEI OFV unnecessary). tutorial’s fitting chunks use pk_est(method = "focei") initial structural screening speed switch "saem_focei" final confirmation.

title: Iterative population PK modeling with poppkflow
text: call pk_run() performs six steps: Compiles specification nlmixr2 code. Validates required data columns computes run_key generated code hash, data hash, estimation settings hash. Checks ledger cache: identical completed run exists parent (cache = "same_parent", default), pk_run() returns run reference immediately without refitting. Pass cache = "" reuse identical model regardless parent (logs cache_hit event events.csv), refit = TRUE force fresh fit. Registers run status = "running", parent_id, stage, note, hashes, software versions (nlmixr2est, rxode2, poppkflow, R). Fits model saves fit.rds, result.rds, diag.rds. fit post-fit storage fails—interrupt session—.exit() handler marks run status = "failed" error message ledger never accumulates stuck "running" rows. Updates ledger row "completed" OFV, dofv_parent, AIC, BIC, parameter counts, condition number, covariance step status, maximum ETA shrinkage, flag count. Let’s fit three nested structural models: 1-compartment (r1), 2-compartment (r2), 2-compartment absorption lag time (r3): Notice pk_inits_from(r2): copies final structural estimates, IIV variances, block covariances, residual error SDs, non-fixed covariate parameters r2 new candidate, letting pk_set_inits() supply initial value newly added tlag.
code: est_fast <- pk_est(method = "focei")  # Run 1: 1-compartment oral base model r1 <- pk_run(   spec_1cmt,   est = est_fast,   note = "1-CMT oral base, IIV on CL and V, prop error",   stage = "structural" )  # Run 2: 2-compartment oral model derived from r1 r2 <- r1 |>   pk_set_structure(ncmt = 2) |>   pk_add_iiv("v2") |>   pk_set_inits(ka = 1, cl = 5, v2 = 30, q = 4, v3 = 50) |>   pk_run(     est = est_fast,     note = "2-CMT oral, IIV on CL and V2, prop error",     stage = "structural"   )  # Run 3: add absorption lag time, initialized from r2's final estimates r3 <- r2 |>   pk_set_structure(lag = TRUE) |>   pk_inits_from(r2) |>   pk_set_inits(tlag = 0.25) |>   pk_run(     est = est_fast,     note = "Add absorption lag time (alag)",     stage = "structural"   )

what: Manual covariate addition vs. automated SCM
title: Iterative population PK modeling with poppkflow
text: can add covariates manually pk_add_cov()—supports four forms: "power": theta * log(COV / ref) (standard allometry continuous power models; set fix = TRUE fixed allometric exponents 0.75 CL 1.0 V2), "linear": theta * (COV - ref), "cat": theta * COV (0/1-coded indicator variables; 1/2-coded covariates FOOD crossover_pk.csv, use form = "linear", ref = 1 form = "custom"), "custom": arbitrary expression given via term theta. systematic testing, pk_scm() runs forward inclusion followed backward elimination directly ledger: Every trial model regular run runs.csv stage = "scm" current step’s model parent. forward step, candidate largest OFV drop exceeding 1-df chi-square threshold forward_p (default 0.01, dOFV < -6.63) included (optionally requiring successful covariance step via require_cov_step = TRUE). backward step, included covariates removed one time; one smallest OFV increase threshold backward_p (default 0.001, dOFV < 10.83) eliminated. decide_trials = TRUE (default), non-selected trial runs automatically marked "rejected" exact dOFV rationale, runs along selected path stay "pending" analyst makes final decision. full step table saved scm/scm01.rds. SCM completes, inspect final model (scm$final), compare base stochastic model (r6), check diagnostics, record decision:
code: cov_cands <- tibble::tribble(   ~param, ~covariate, ~form   , ~ref, ~init,   "cl"  , "WT"      , "power" , 70  , 0.75 ,   "cl"  , "CRCL"    , "power" , 100 , 0.3  ,   "cl"  , "AGE"     , "linear", 50  , 0    ,   "cl"  , "SEXF"    , "cat"   , NA  , 0    ,   "v2"  , "WT"      , "power" , 70  , 1.0  ,   "v2"  , "SEXF"    , "cat"   , NA  , 0 )  scm <- pk_scm(   base = r6,   candidates = cov_cands,   est = est_fast,   require_cov_step = FALSE ) scm scm$steps r_final_focei <- scm$final pk_compare(r6, r_final_focei, ref = "first") pk_params_table(r_final_focei) pk_diagnostics(r_final_focei, plots = TRUE)  # Confirm the final covariate model with the default SAEM -> FOCEI strategy r_final <- r_final_focei |>   pk_inits_from(r_final_focei) |>   pk_run(     est = pk_est(method = "saem_focei", seed = 2026, nBurn = 200, nEm = 200),     note = "Final covariate model confirmed with SAEM -> FOCEI",     stage = "final"   )  pk_decide(   r_final,   "accepted",   reason = "Final covariate model (WT and CRCL on CL, WT on V2) confirmed with SAEM->FOCEI; clean diagnostics" )
